Plot conditional mean trajectories (CMT)

Source: R/cmtPlot.R
cmtPlot.Rd

This function generates the Conditional Mean Trajectories (CMT) plot: the mean biomarker trajectory of the patients whose event happened in the window (condi_time2event - event_window, condi_time2event]. The time from the first measurement up to condi_time2event is cut into consecutive intervals of length interval_time; each point is the mean of those patients' biomarker values measured within one interval, plotted at the interval's end, and a straight line is fitted through the points. With competing risks there is one trajectory per event type.

All times – time_variable, survival_variable, condi_time2event, event_window and interval_time – are in the units of the data (years, months, days, ...), and the time axis shows time_variable on that scale, labelled with its name.

Only patients with an observed event enter: with competing risks, those whose event_type_variable equals one of event_type; without, those whose status_variable is not 0. Without competing risks and with status_variable = NULL, patients are selected by their survival time alone, so censored ones are included too, with a warning. An interval without any measurement is left out rather than filled in.

Usage

cmtPlot(
  data_plot_all,
  condi_time2event,
  event_type_variable,
  event_type,
  bio_variable,
  time_variable,
  survival_variable,
  interval_time = 1/12,
  id_variable = "id",
  status_variable = NULL,
  event_window = 1
)

Arguments

data_plot_all

A data.frame that includes the biomarker used for plotting. It is utilized to plot conditional mean trajectories (CMT).

condi_time2event

Event time the patients are selected around. If NULL, it defaults to the midpoint of the observed range of time_variable in data_plot_all.

event_type_variable

Competing risks variable indicator name. Set to NULL if there are no competing risks.

event_type

A vector containing the values of event_type_variable for the event types to plot (at least two).

bio_variable

Name of the biomarker variable used for plotting.

time_variable

The name of time variable in linear mixed model.

survival_variable

Name of the time-to-event outcomes variable.

interval_time

Length of the intervals the follow-up is cut into, in the units of time_variable.

id_variable

Name of the patient ID column in data_plot_all. Default is "id".

status_variable

Without competing risks, the name of the event indicator (0 = censored), so that only patients with an event are used. Ignored with competing risks.

event_window

Width of the window of event times before condi_time2event that a patient's event must fall in, in the units of survival_variable. Default 1 (one year for data in years; use e.g. 12 for months or 365 for days).

Value

Conditional mean trajectories plot.

Examples


# example without competing risks

data(pbc3)

pbc.cmt <- cmtPlot(data_plot_all = pbc3, condi_time2event = 5,
   event_type_variable = NULL, event_type = NULL,
   bio_variable = "serBilir", time_variable = "year",
   survival_variable = "years",
   interval_time = 1/12, status_variable = "status3"
)

pbc.cmt



# example with competing risks

data(pbc3)

pbc.cmt.cr <- cmtPlot(pbc3, condi_time2event = 5,
   event_type_variable = 'status4', event_type = c("0", "1"),
   bio_variable = "albumin", time_variable = "year",
   survival_variable = "years",
   interval_time = 1/4
)

pbc.cmt.cr
